summary: 11 comment-endorsed recommendations across developer tools, reading, offline dictation, and educational media.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 past front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Sashiko
items.source_story_title: Why isn't the industry freaking out about DeepSeek 4.1 Flash?
items.summary: AI code-review system praised for kernel reviews; watch token spending.
items.why_included: Concrete first-hand use comes with a useful operating-cost warning.
items.evidence: A contributor used Sashiko locally before submitting Linux kernel changes and praised the system, while warning that it consumes many tokens.

evidence_sources.author: eru
evidence_sources.excerpt: Eg I've used Sashiko locally for Linux kernel code reviews before sending out my contributions out to the world. Sashiko is a great system, but it can burn through tokens like there's no tomorrow.

items.name: Embedded Swift
items.source_story_title: A minimal kernel in Swift, running in QEMU
items.summary: Swift for bare-metal systems, praised for straightforward C/C++ interoperability.
items.why_included: A boot-firmware experiment supplies practical evidence beyond enthusiasm for the submitted kernel.
items.evidence: A commenter who wrote simulator boot firmware praised Embedded Swift's out-of-the-box C/C++ interoperability and ease of adoption.

evidence_sources.author: aseipp
evidence_sources.excerpt: But beyond that I think the best feature is that the C/C++ interop works really well and comes out of the box. Makes two-way adoption easy. I wrote a small boot firmware for a simulator

items.name: Uxn
items.summary: Tiny portable virtual machine for building deliberately small, durable applications.
items.why_included: The comment independently praises a specific project rather than merely admiring off-grid living.
items.evidence: A fan singles out Uxn and its applications, praising how much a small, portable virtual machine can accomplish.

evidence_sources.author: larme
evidence_sources.excerpt: Always a fan of their works, especially uxn[0] and apps developed for it. They showcase how many things a small virtual machine can do while being very portable

items.name: datafusion-ducklake
items.summary: DuckLake integration for Apache DataFusion, with a PostgreSQL-backed catalog option.
items.why_included: An independent endorsement is supplemented by clearly labeled implementer experience.
items.evidence: A commenter praises the alternate Rust/DataFusion initiative. An implementer reports performance matching their specialized catalogs and praises PostgreSQL as the catalog store.

evidence_sources.author: smithclay
evidence_sources.excerpt: There's a cool alternate rust/datafusion ecosystem initiative going on at

evidence_sources.author: eddietejeda
evidence_sources.excerpt: Since Ducklake is only a spec, we implemented datafusion-ducklake, and it performs as well as any custom or specialized catalog we built. We use Postgres as the catalog store, and it does not get much simpler than that: a transactional database for transactional data.

items.name: Holesail
items.source_story_title: Dat-ecosystem: high level applications built on top of P2P protocols
items.summary: Open-source P2P reverse proxy recommended for trying NAT-traversing connections.
items.why_included: An explicit try-it recommendation points to a concrete P2P application.
items.evidence: In response to doubts about NAT traversal, a commenter recommends trying Holesail to see P2P hole punching in action.

evidence_sources.author: schmoooo
evidence_sources.excerpt: if you dont want to dive that deep, just try something like https://holesail.io first to see that holepunching nat traversing p2p is real

items.name: Zotero
items.source_story_title: The Slow Formation of Durable Software
items.summary: Research library for collecting, annotating, and syncing articles and books.
items.why_included: An independent comment explicitly recommends the story subject with detailed daily-use evidence.
items.evidence: A daily user praises Zotero's article snapshots, annotation workflow, and cross-device sync.

evidence_sources.author: nickledave
evidence_sources.excerpt: It also does an amazing job of taking snapshots of posts. I use it all the time to grab posts from HackerNews so I can mark them up. And it automagically syncs everywhere across devices

items.name: wallabag
items.source_story_title: The Slow Formation of Durable Software
items.summary: Self-hosted read-it-later app; a user praises syncing across personal devices.
items.why_included: A happy self-hosting user offers a concrete reading-workflow alternative.
items.evidence: A commenter uses a locally hosted wallabag instance across computers and a smartphone and reports being happy with it.

evidence_sources.author: Shorel
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use a locally hosted Wallabag, synchronized with all my computers, smartphone, etc. Maybe Zotero does more than Wallabag, but I am happy with it so far.

items.name: FUTO Keyboard
items.source_story_title: Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB
items.summary: Offline Android keyboard praised for dictation accuracy; source-available, not open-source.
items.why_included: A long-time user's clear approval supports resurfacing after the 90-day cooldown.
items.evidence: A long-time user praises on-device speech recognition accuracy and says they love the keyboard. Their edit clarifies that its license is source-available rather than open-source.

evidence_sources.author: rpdillon
evidence_sources.excerpt: FUTO keyboard (open-source, free) runs entirely on-device and has extremely good STT accurary, especially with the 70M parameter model. I've used it for years now and love it.

evidence_sources.author: robertlane0
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'd classify it as "source-available" given the noncommercial clause in the license.

items.name: Clickspring
items.source_story_title: Archaeologists Are Reconstructing the 'Invisible' Technologies of the Stone Age
items.summary: Precision-machining videos featuring skeleton clocks and an Antikythera mechanism reconstruction.
items.why_included: An enthusiastic recommendation points to unusually detailed hands-on craft education.
items.evidence: A commenter recommends Clickspring's videos and counts the skeleton-clock build among their favorite pieces of internet content.

evidence_sources.author: MengerSponge
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you've never watched Clickspring's Youtube videos you're in for a treat. He has a long-running series where he works to make a new Antikythera mechanism using ancient (bronze age) technologies.

items.name: Cameras and Lenses
items.source_story_title: Archaeologists Are Reconstructing the 'Invisible' Technologies of the Stone Age
items.summary: Bartosz Ciechanowski's visual explainer builds camera optics from first principles.
items.why_included: Explicit praise links directly to a concrete educational essay.
items.evidence: A commenter places Ciechanowski's webpages alongside their favorite internet content and links specifically to Cameras and Lenses.

evidence_sources.author: MengerSponge
evidence_sources.excerpt: His skeleton clock build is one of my favorite pieces of internet content ever, up there with Bartoz's gorgeous webpages:
